title: 语义能力名注册表
description: The single registry of semantic capability names (contract section 2, the foundation). A task states a semantic need, a node states a semantic capability PLUS the implementation binding that satisfies it, and this file is the only place where the two vocabularies meet. See contracts/README.md §2.2 and decision one. WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: today capability is expressed as a bare package string. The platform's `required_software` vocabulary has 14 members, the client can advertise 5 (`node/git/python3/ffmpeg/ffprobe`), and the intersection is exactly 1 (`ffmpeg`) — so 19 of 25 task types are permanently unreachable for that node (audit §1.1). Sixteen of those names appear ZERO times in the local TypeScript source. The mismatch is not a bug in either side's list; it is the absence of a semantic layer between them.
name_grammar_description: Names are lowercase, dot-separated, and read as domain.object.action (e.g. `ocr.image`, `doc.pdf.extract`, `accelerator.gpu`). A name identifies a CAPABILITY, never a vendor, package, or binary: `media.transcode` must not be called `ffmpeg`. That single rule is what lets the implementation be replaced without renegotiating a single task.
provenance: docs/dev-plan/跨边界一致性审计.md §1.1 — the platform's required_software union (14 names) and the 20 blocked task types, read from engine/task_registry.py plus production database we_workers
docs/dev-plan/evidence/双机验收/AT-08.json — a real dispatcher worker row carrying 47 capability keys, captured 2026-09-17T05:36:48.802Z
packages/host/compute-core/tests/fixtures/platform-worker-capabilities.ts — the 47-key field set pinned locally from that capture
生产库 we_workers 抽样 (审计 §1.1) — a real node advertising 11 Python tier packages, including pdfplumber and tldextract

platform_required_software_description: The union of every TaskTypeSpec.required_software value, read statically from engine/task_registry.py (14 members). This array is the migration target: every member MUST map to at least one implementation below, and the contract test fails if any member is unaccounted for. It is reproduced here so the registry can be checked without reading the platform source.

alias_normalization.description: Real advertisements in the production pool do not agree on separators: one sampled node advertised `faster-whisper` (hyphen) while the platform's required_software says `faster_whisper` (underscore). Any matcher that compares raw strings will miss this. Normalization rule for v1: lowercase, then map `-` to `_`. Aliases are recorded per implementation in `aliases` so the raw advertised value can still be attributed to a real package.

package_index_description: Reverse index from a legacy package/tool name to the capabilities it can satisfy: the migration lookup that answers 'which semantic capability was this required_software value standing in for'. Keys are normalized per alias_normalization. Every value must be exactly the reverse of `capabilities[].implementations[].package_names`; the contract test asserts both directions so a one-way reference cannot appear. Covers all 14 members of platform_required_software plus the three OCR implementations the brief adds (paddleocr, rapidocr, pytesseract) and pdfplumber, which is observed in production advertisements but never required. 18 keys total.

platform_vocabulary_observed.name: media.probe
platform_vocabulary_observed.note: The platform already uses a dot-name for this concept; this registry uses the same spelling. This is direct evidence that dot-names are the platform's own convention, not something this draft invents.

platform_vocabulary_observed.name: doc.pdf.text
platform_vocabulary_observed.note: The platform has a dot-name doc.pdf.text where this registry says doc.pdf.extract. Only two members of the platform's CAPABILITIES set were visible from this repository, so the full set could not be read. RECONCILIATION IS REQUIRED BEFORE ADOPTION: either this registry adopts the platform's exact names, or the platform publishes the mapping. Guessing which is authoritative is exactly the failure mode this contract exists to prevent.

open_questions.question: Are multiple `implementations` of one capability alternatives (OR) or a required set (AND)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Legacy `required_software` is an AND-set: planner.py:717-731 hard-filters on `effective_needed.issubset(worker_sw)`. A registry `implementations` list reads naturally as 'any one suffices' (OR). For ocr.image and speech.transcribe OR is almost certainly right (three OCR engines, two whisper variants). For web.fetch the legacy set demanded requests AND selectolax together, and for image_caption it demanded moondream2 AND pillow — there the AND is real, because an HTTP client and an HTML parser are not alternatives.
open_questions.status: UNRESOLVED. This draft encodes both facts (the list, plus a per-implementation `role`) and does not pick a matching rule. Picking one without the platform's confirmation would trade a visible divergence (no semantic layer) for an invisible one (a semantic layer that silently drops half of an AND-set).

open_questions.question: Which side owns the semantic name space — this registry or engine/capabilities.py?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Two registries would be a sixth copy of a vocabulary, which is the exact defect class being fixed (audit §1.1, §1.11: three copies of the tool list).
open_questions.status: UNRESOLVED. Only two platform names are observable from this repository (doc.pdf.text, media.probe). Proposal for phase 2: the platform's CAPABILITIES set becomes the single source and this file is generated from it, with the legacy package mapping retained as the migration lookup.

open_questions.question: What is the versioning unit for min_version?
open_questions.why_it_matters: task.requires[].min_version is declared to mean 'generation of the capability contract'. Whether a capability name can be versioned independently of the whole v1 contract is not decidable from the evidence read.
open_questions.status: UNRESOLVED; v1 treats min_version as advisory and does not enforce it.
